frameworks.name: Club-Based Tournament Model
frameworks.definition: A revenue model where tournaments are set up via local soccer-club partnerships; clubs provide fields and marketing, the operator handles everything else including team registration and tournament logistics.

frameworks.name: National Scalable Tournament Operations
frameworks.definition: A structure where a single operator runs tournaments at scale (1000+/year) by partnering with clubs in multiple geographies rather than owning fields or operating single locations.

claims.text: When founder shifts to leadership level and removes themselves from day-to-day operations, the primary challenge becomes distributing their tacit knowledge and systems throughout the organization rather than executing directly.
claims.speaker: Unknown founder (soccer tournaments)
conditions: business has systems and operations that can continue without founder
claims.mechanism: Without documented systems, founder knowledge remains bottlenecked in founder's head
bounded_by: Does not apply when business is early-stage founder-dependent

claims.text: The business can grow 50% per year and has been growing at that rate for five years, scaling from lower base to ~$1.5M current revenue, targeting $15M revenue within four years (implying ~3x annual growth required).
claims.speaker: Unknown founder (soccer tournaments)

numbers.axis: annual revenue growth rate and absolute revenue targets

claims.text: The business has achieved 30% gross margins at ~$1.5M revenue, operates with systems and processes capable of running 1000 tournaments annually, but is constrained by manpower (team depth and host-club partner network density) not by operations or systems capability.
claims.speaker: Unknown founder (soccer tournaments)
claims.mechanism: Operations systematization allows owner to take 2-4 weeks off while business continues; margins at 30% enable reinvestment; the true constraint is sales capacity (teams/clubs acquisition) not fulfillment
bounded_by: Assumes operations are truly documented and transferable

claims.text: The team has a huge database of clubs and only recently (a couple months prior) started paid advertising, indicating most lead flow has been organic/database-driven with untapped upside in paid channels.
claims.speaker: Unknown founder (soccer tournaments)
claims.mechanism: Organic reach is maxed out; paid ads create new inbound without cannibalizing existing channel

claims.text: In this tournament/club model, the president serves as both the chief operating officer (running everything) and the lead salesperson, but he is capacity-constrained to five sales calls per day, creating a sales bottleneck despite ample inbound lead flow.
claims.speaker: Unknown founder (soccer tournaments) and unnamed advisor
conditions: person serving dual role of operator and salesperson
more lead flow than one person can convert
claims.mechanism: One person cannot scale beyond personal sales capacity (5 calls/day); removing them from sales frees operator time but loses sales capacity unless replaced with specialized salespeople

numbers.axis: sales capacity per person per day

claims.text: Scaling a service business from $1.5M to $15M (10x revenue growth in 4 years) with current systems and margins requires first hiring additional salespeople to convert the available lead flow, not expanding operations or changing pricing.
claims.speaker: Unnamed advisor (Hormozi or similar)
claims.mechanism: Sales capacity is the constraint; hiring salespeople directly increases revenue conversion of existing inbound; each new salesperson multiplies output by their personal capacity (5 calls/day)

claims.text: The founder should spend the next period recruiting sales staff through outreach and market sourcing rather than managing operations or corporate initiatives, because sales capacity is the binding constraint on growth.
claims.speaker: Unnamed advisor
conditions: founder is bored and looking for highest-leverage activity
claims.mechanism: Sales hiring creates a 5x multiplier on business output (5 salespeople × 5 calls/day each); other activities do not have comparable leverage

examples.text: The founder has been able to take 2-4 weeks off while the business continues to operate and generate revenue (~$500k profit margin while away), demonstrating that the business model and operations are not founder-dependent for execution.

The business partners with local soccer clubs across the country (national footprint); each club provides fields and assists with marketing to their members. The operator recruits teams from the clubs for the tournament, collects registration fees, and handles all logistics.

Despite having abundant inbound lead flow from the club database and only recently starting paid ads (a couple months prior), the sales bottleneck remains at 5 calls per day from the president/operator, creating a direct constraint on revenue growth.

practices.text: When a founder is constrained by dual roles (COO + sales), remove them from the sales function and hire dedicated salespeople to manage the lead flow they have already developed.
Establish a recruiting and compensation strategy for sales staff as a formal organizational function (career path, recruiting, onboarding, management) rather than ad hoc hiring.
Use the team-scale analogy: if you have a five-person sales team and add another five, the business can compete and scale at 2x pace, with each salesperson capable of five calls per day.
